transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-05-26
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Redwood SRE); Dana Ortiz (Mistral Health CTO), Samir Patel (Mistral ML Eng), Lena Morales (Infra Lead), Ravi Kapoor (SecOps)

Summary:
- High-level discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming and burst scenarios, concurrency requirements, and tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable burst SLA but wants a pilot on Hosted to validate token/sec and streaming behavior.

Topics:
- p95 targets (100-200ms vs 400-800ms depending on model size)
- concurrency and token/sec during peaks
- streaming vs batching tradeoffs
- data residency, KMS, and audit logging
- pilot scope and benchmarks

Action items noted during call below.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick intros?
[00:12] Dana: Hi all, Dana Ortiz from Mistral Health, I run platform and infra for the product team.
[00:18] Samir: Samir here, ML, we own the model infra and evals.
[00:24] Lena: Lena, infra lead, I'll be owning any private or VPC set up.
[00:30] Jordan: Great, and Priya and Marco from our side, Priya will do the deep dive. We're here to understand your p95 and throughput needs, and then propose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, right?
[00:45] Priya: Yep. Can you share rough numbers: p95 goal, concurrency, and typical request size in tokens?
[00:52] Samir: Sure, our baseline is a 256-token input, average output 180 tokens. In steady state we do about 40 rps, but the issue is bursts — we see 400 rps for short windows (1-3 minutes) during nightly batch+ingestion and user surges.
[01:12] Jordan: OK, so 40 steady and 400 during bursts, got it. And p95 target?
[01:18] Dana: For user-facing chat we want p95 under 350ms ideally. For high-complexity summaries we're OK with up to 800ms if quality is better.
[01:28] Priya: That's helpful. When you say 400 rps burst, is that concurrent streaming sessions or many short requests?
[01:35] Samir: Mix — about 60% are streaming token streams, the rest are standard generation. Streaming tends to run longer tokens, so tokens/sec load's high.
[01:45] Marco: When you say streaming, do you mean server-sent events style, or websockets with chunked tokens?
[01:50] Samir: Websockets mostly. We need low tail latency because the UI shows progressive tokens.
[02:00] Priya: OK. Two main levers: Dedicated reserved GPU pool gives predictable latency for bursts; Hosted can handle it with autoscaling but cold starts and quotas sometimes make the p95 bounce. Private gives you full control but we have to package and manage the infra.
[02:18] Lena: Our security team prefers Dedicated or Private due to PHI concerns; Hosted is allowed if we can guarantee encryption at rest and bring-your-own-key.
[02:28] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS for Hosted via our enterprise plan, plus audit logs per-token. We'll share the SOC2/ISO summary after.
[02:36] Ravi: Important for us: KMS key rotation and HSM compatibility. Does Redwood integrate with HSM-backed KMS?
[02:44] Priya: Yes, we support common KMS providers and HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated, Hosted with BYOK in the enterprise tier. We'll post the integration notes.
[02:54] Samir: On the perf side, do you have token/sec benchmarks for 13B and 70B models? Our experiments vary.
[03:02] Priya: We do. Quick nuance: 70B in fp16 or quantized modes behaves differently. For streaming p95 at 350ms you typically need batching tuned and KV cache warm — that favors Dedicated.
[03:18] Jordan: Also worth noting that our runtime can route to compatible model variants if capacity's constrained — automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants.
[03:28] Dana: What's the trade-off cost-wise for that? We don't want noticeable quality regression.
[03:34] Marco: We can set fallback policies per-route with quality thresholds. If quality fall below X we can fail open to a canary or reject, depends on your tolerance.
[03:44] Samir: For benchmarking what should we collect? Token histograms, seq lengths, concurrency distribution?
[03:50] Priya: Yes, a traffic profile CSV with timestamp, request_type (stream/gen), tokens_in, tokens_out, latency at current infra. Also target SLOs and failure modes. We'll run a two-phase benchmark: steady-state and burst-surge patterns.
[04:05] Samir: We can produce that. We also have a synthetic harness that can replay traffic to a URL. Can Redwood consume that or do you want us to run locally?
[04:14] Priya: We can ingest the harness but prefer running on our side against a temporary Dedicated pilot to eliminate network variance. If you want to run it against Hosted we can do that too.
[04:26] Lena: How quickly can we get a Dedicated pilot? We have approvals for a short-term reserved pool.
[04:32] Jordan: Typically we can spin a small Dedicated pool within a week — depends on cloud region and GPU type. We should pick instance type: A100 or H100. Which do you prefer?
[04:42] Samir: A100s are fine. H100 would be great but cost-prohibitive for pilots.
[04:48] Priya: Note: H100 shows advantages on longer sequences with Flash attention kernels; A100s give strong all-around perf. For 256+180 tokens A100 is a solid baseline.
[04:59] Dana: Regarding p95 numbers, can you quote an expected p95 for 13B vs 70B on A100 with streaming? Ballpark.
[05:06] Priya: Ballpark: 13B streaming p95 ~120-220ms depending on concurrency; 70B quantized could be 300-900ms depending on quant and KV cache warm. These are rough; we'll run the actual run.
[05:20] Samir: That's promising. For our client embeddings pipeline we run batch 10K requests at night — need to ensure that doesn't interfere with user chat.
[05:28] Marco: We can dedicate separate pools or set priority routing. Dedicated allows strict isolation. On Hosted we can use routing policies to separate embedding jobs to cheaper models or off-peak times.
[05:40] Ravi: For encryption in transit and at rest, any PCI/PHI specific controls we should be aware of?
[05:46] Jordan: We have TLS enforced in transit and at-rest encryption. For PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with BYOK and VPC peering for extra controls.
[05:56] Samir: Let's talk concurrency: you mentioned continuous batching — will that hurt streaming latency?
[06:03] Priya: Continuous batching aggregates small requests to increase throughput; for streaming we do micro-batching and ensure early flush for the first tokens to keep tail low. It's a balance configured per-model/route.
[06:16] Lena: If we go Private, what's the management overhead? We're small ops.
[06:21] Marco: Private is heavier: deployable as a packaged runtime with orchestration; you manage the nodes, but we provide automation and an ops runbook. For low ops customers we recommend Dedicated.
[06:35] Dana: Fine. Our timeline: pilot in early June, production by end of Q3, budget approvals expected next week.
[06:44] Jordan: Good. We'll prioritize a Dedicated pilot for you with A100s and run the prescribed steady and burst tests.
[06:50] Samir: On model variants, can you host our custom fine-tuned 13B? Licensing-wise?
[06:56] Priya: Yes, we onboard custom models; there's a model onboarding checklist. For private data we recommend model version pinning and restricted access.
[07:06] Samir: OK.
[07:12] Jordan: Let's capture next steps — Priya, you'll own the benchmark plan and sample script; Jordan will follow up on commercials; Lena will send traffic profile.
[07:22] Priya: I'll share a benchmark matrix with steady/burst scenar and a k6-style harness example. Note: we'll include warm-up runs to prime KV cache.
[07:34] Lena: I'll export token histograms and a 7-day sample of peaks.
[07:40] Dana: Security wants a doc on KMS keys and HSM compatibility.
[07:44] Ravi: And an SLA doc with fallbacks and audit logs.
[07:48] Jordan: We'll send SOC2 summary and an HSM/KMS integration note; also the pilot pricing and a sample SLA. Expect arcs from me by EOW.
[07:58] Samir: One quick question — during bursts, if Dedicated pool saturates, what's the behavior? Does Redwood auto-burst to cloud-hosted spare capacity?
[08:06] Priya: We can configure burst policies: either queue, fail, or fallback to Hosted smaller model. For mission-critical chat we recommend fallback to a canary quantized variant with monitored quality regression.
[08:20] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?
[08:23] Dana: Not now. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Next Steps (as discussed):
- Priya to send benchmark plan, sample harness, and expected p95 targets per model (Due 2027-06-02).
- Jordan to send pilot pricing options and SOC2/KMS summary (Due 2027-06-04).
- Lena to provide token distribution CSV and peak traffic capture (Due 2027-05-31).
- Set up Dedicated pilot (2 x A100) for week of 2027-06-07 pending approvals.

Links referenced:
